mercy_translation.text:
When did human beings begin to abandon the worship of idols except from the time the true Word of God came among human beings? When did the oracles among the Greeks and everywhere cease and become empty except when the Savior manifested himself even upon earth?

When did the gods and heroes celebrated by poets begin to be condemned as merely mortal human beings except from the time the Lord accomplished the trophy over death and preserved the body he had taken incorruptible by raising it from the dead?

When was the deception and madness of demons despised except when the Power of God, the Word, Master of all these things, condescended because of human weakness and appeared on earth? When did the art and schools of magic begin to be trampled down except when the divine manifestation of the Word took place among human beings?

And in general, when did the wisdom of the Greeks become foolish except when the true Wisdom of God manifested himself on earth? Formerly the whole inhabited world and every place wandered in the worship of idols, and people considered nothing but the idols to be gods. But now throughout the whole inhabited world people abandon the superstition of idols and flee to Christ. Worshiping him as God, they come through him to know the Father whom they did not know.

And what is remarkable is that although there were different and countless objects of worship, each place having its own idol, and the one called a god among them being unable to pass beyond the neighboring district so as to persuade even nearby people to worship him, but scarcely being worshiped even in his own territory—since no one worshiped the god of his neighbor but each guarded his own idol, supposing it to be lord of all—Christ alone is worshiped by all, one and the same everywhere.

What the weakness of idols could not accomplish even with those living nearby, Christ has accomplished, persuading not only neighbors but simply the whole inhabited world to worship one and the same Lord, and through him God his Father.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Athanasius contrasts the local cults of antiquity with what he perceives as the universal spread of Christian worship.
This is an apologetic observation from late antiquity and should be contextualized historically.
